prediction.likelyOutcome: The tenants are likely to prevail on their repair-and-maintenance and insurance covenant breach counterclaims (roughly $17,950 + $1,415 as testified), while Griffith's $25,000 roof-damage claim and his fraud/oral-lease theories face serious liability problems given his own maintenance default and the integrated written lease. Net, the case should resolve in the tenants' favor in the high-teens-to-low-twenties range on the damages actually quantified in this record, with the option-to-purchase breach and Rule 68 fee-shifting as unquantified upside not yet reflected in the range.

issues.label: Rule 68 Offer of Judgment / Fee-Shifting Exposure

outcome.description: After a two-day bench trial the court held the written lease governed, found the landlord breached its insurance and maintenance covenants, and awarded the tenants $19,330 in damages (2016-2017 insurance premiums and the 2016 roof-failure repair and painting costs; earlier claims were time-barred), dismissed the landlord's claims, and awarded the tenants $59,604.75 in attorney's fees under Civil Rule 68, for a final judgment of $85,895.62. The Alaska Supreme Court affirmed on December 16, 2022.
